title: Group Orders by Month Using DATE_TRUNC
description:
Write a query to count orders and total revenue **per calendar month**. Use `DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)` to truncate each date to its month. Return `month`, `order_count`, and `total_amount`, ordered by `month`.

**Table: orders**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| customer_id | INT |
| order_date | DATE |
| amount | DECIMAL |
solution_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(amount) AS total_amount FROM orders GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) ORDER BY month

test_cases.description: Returns 3 rows: July (2 orders), August (3 orders), September (3 orders)

hints: `DATE_TRUNC('month', date)` rounds a date down to the first day of its month (e.g., 2026-07-15 → 2026-07-01).
This is a PostgreSQL function. In MySQL use `DATE_FORMAT(order_date, '%Y-%m-01')` for the same effect.
explanation: `DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)` normalises dates to month start. Grouping on this expression creates 3 month buckets: July (2 orders, $350), August (3 orders, $725), September (3 orders, $875).
